chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Suleyman ibn Rushayd, from his father, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

I ate in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so a variety of food was brought to him. He said: 'Eat from this.' As for me, there is nothing more beloved to me than al-tharid, and I wish that al-isfanajat had been forbidden.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الثَّرِيد: A dish of bread soaked in meat broth, highly preferred by the Imams
key_terms.الْإِسْفَانَاجَات: A spinach dish, noted for reducing appetite

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq prefer to eat and what did he wish was forbidden?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s personal culinary preference for *tharid* (bread soaked in broth) while expressing a desire for the prohibition of *isfanajat* (likely spinach or a similar leafy green), reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving legal and health rulings from the Prophet’s and Imams’ daily habits (*sunan*). The mention of specific foods illustrates the concept of *takhassus* (specificity) in the Imams' tastes, distinguishing their personal preferences from obligatory religious rulings, and offers insight into the dietary practices of the Ahl al-Bayt during the Abbasid era.
